summary: Former Shenandoah National Park lookout on Trayfoot Mountain, Rockingham County, VA; listed as gone; the summit is a hike-in clearing today.

facts.design: Metal live-in cab tower with catwalk (last tower; hobbyist description written from memory)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; a hiking guide says only a fading clearing marks the summit

access.note: Reached on foot by park trails from the Blackrock Summit parking area

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 miles one way with roughly 625 feet of climbing; no open views from the summit

evidence.supports: last tower was a metal live-in cab tower with catwalk
evidence.quote: The final tower on this site was a metal live in cab tower with catwalk.

evidence.supports: large tank on the ground below the tower
evidence.quote: It had a big submarine looking tank on the ground below the tower.

evidence.supports: description written from memory of a park archive photo
evidence.quote: written from memory of a photo in the park archives

evidence.supports: in Rockingham County, inside Shenandoah National Park
fire lookout once on the summit; only a clearing left
evidence.quote: There used to be a fire lookout there, but all signs of it are gone except for a vanishing clearing.

evidence.supports: park had six fire lookouts within its boundaries
evidence.quote: Shenandoah National Park had 6 fire lookouts within the boundaries.

evidence.supports: Trayfoot Mountain listed among park lookouts
park stopped regularly manning its five towers by the late 1950s
evidence.quote: Shenandoah National Park stopped regularly manning its five lookout towers by the late 1950s.

evidence.supports: early 1960s dismantle, scrap or sell the park's towers
evidence.quote: By the early 1960s, the park began to dismantle, scrap, or sell the five lookout towers it had at that time.

evidence.supports: listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association
no structure or footings described; only a clearing

evidence.quote: Hike from the Blackrock Summit parking area

evidence.quote: There are no unobstructed views there

notes_for_editor: No build year and no removal year appear in any source found. The late-1950s and early-1960s dates come from WillhiteWeb's park-wide account, which does not say which tower went when, so they are not Trayfoot's own dates. The cab description is from memory, per its author. Access 'public' is inferred from the park trail network; no park page confirmed the summit route. Check the NPS Shenandoah archives for build and removal years.
